sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic check only: OLAC lists nothing but Glottolog and Ethnologue entries; Glottolog has zero grammar/phonology/sketch references (only overviews and wordlists: Piron 1997, Williamson 1973, Williamson & Shimizu 1968, Wente-Lukas 1985, Meek 1931, Blench 2006, 2016).

sources.citation: Angitso, Michael T. & Roland Kiessling. 2024. Towards reconstructing the numeral classifier system of Proto-Tivoid. Afrika und Uebersee 97: 204-232. doi:10.15460/auue.2024.97.1.329
sources.note: Checked for new Batu sources: contains no Batu data and cites no Batu description (Tiv, Ugare, Iyive etc. only); nothing on stress. Not retained held by the project.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2016. New research on Tivoid and its place within Bantoid. Slides presented at Bantu 6, University of Helsinki, 20-22 June 2016.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; Batu mentioned only for classification/population; mentions tonal alternation in Tivoid verb/noun morphology generally (Iyive, Iceve), not Batu.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. [2016]. The Tivoid languages: Overview and Comparative Word List. Circulation draft, ms. (Glottolog ref 78922)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; Batu appears only in the classification history and Table 1 (source: Koops ms.). Only prosodic remark is that Tiv and Ugare are two-tone languages and Esimbi has three tones; Batu not mentioned there.

sources.citation: Starr, Alan & Clark Regnier. 2008 [1990]. Tivoid survey. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2008-022.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Batu content at all (Cameroon-side Tivoid only); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger M. 2006 [printout Nov. 2010]. Wordlists of Batu, Kamino and Buru languages spoken in southern Taraba State, Nigeria. Data collected by Robert Koops in the 1970s, typed by Emma Connell, revised and converted to Unicode by R. Blench. Ms., Kay Williamson Educational Foundation, Cambridge. 14 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Two-page intro (classification only) plus a tone-marked comparative wordlist (Afi/Amanda, Kamino, Buru, Manta, Tiv). Intro p.1 notes: 'Robert Koops also prepared a typescript on Batu phonemes, which I hope to incorporate in a later version.'

sources.citation: Piron, Pascale. 1997. Classification interne du groupe bantoide. 2 vols. (LINCOM Studies in African Linguistics 11-12.) Muenchen: Lincom Europa.

sources.note: Lexicostatistical classification including Batu; may contain brief notes on transcription/tone of the Batu list, but not a phonological description.

sources.citation: Koops, Robert. n.d. [1970s]. Batu phonemes. Unpublished typescript (referred to in Blench 2006:1: 'Robert Koops also prepared a typescript on Batu phonemes').
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only known phonological analysis of Batu; if it has a suprasegmentals section it would be the sole first-hand statement on tone/stress. Possibly held by R. Blench (Kay Williamson Educational Foundation) or in Koops's papers (SIL Nigeria / NBTT, Jos).

sources.citation: Meek, Charles K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria. 2 vols. London: Kegan Paul, Trench, Trubner. Vol. II pp. 565-569, 586-589 (Batu notes and vocabulary).
